messages.content: Write a job posting for a senior backend engineer at a mid-sized fintech company. Around 250 words.

**Senior Backend Engineer**
Remote (US) or Chicago office · $180k–$215k + equity

We move money for about 40,000 small businesses. Payroll clears, invoices settle, and ACH files go out on a schedule that doesn't care whether our on-call engineer is having a bad week. The backend team is nine people. We're hiring a tenth.

What you'd work on: the ledger service and the payment orchestration layer built around it. Go and Postgres, plus an old Python service still handling reconciliation that someone will need to retire at some point. Recent wins: settlement latency dropped from 90 seconds to under 10, and we rewrote our idempotency handling after a rough week in March exposed where our thinking had been off.

We're looking for roughly six years of backend experience, some of it on systems where correctness mattered more than speed. Payments experience helps but isn't required; people arriving from billing, inventory, or any double-entry domain tend to ramp quickly. You should want to own a service end to end, pager and all.

Honestly, the rough parts: we're regulated, so there's compliance work, and audit season drags. Our test suite takes 14 minutes. The reconciliation path has debt we're paying down gradually rather than in one push.

The good parts: small team, real ownership, no one between you and a deploy. We ship most days. Code review is thorough without getting personal.

How hiring works: a screen, a systems design conversation, a paid take-home, and a chat with the team. Four to five hours spread over two weeks.
